summary:
The biggest opportunity today is retatrutide versus semaglutide 2 mg in TRANSCEND-T2D-2, published Oct 28, 2026, and I checked the numbers against Lilly's press release. It is the first Phase 3 randomized head-to-head of retatrutide against another incretin, so it meets every Lane C rule: public within 48 h, a named next-gen drug, a headline efficacy number, and a semaglutide arm.
- **Trial:** 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes, open-label, 80 weeks, retatrutide 9 or 12 mg versus Ozempic 2 mg.
- **Results:** A1C fell 2.2% versus 1.8%. Weight fell 19.5–20.9% versus 9.4%. These use the "if everyone stayed on treatment" measure, and they are company topline results, not yet peer-reviewed.
- **Downsides to report:** more people stopped because of side effects (4.8% and 7.9% versus 2.7%), and dysesthesia (abnormal skin sensations) was more common (4.8% and 6.5% versus 2.7%).

ABC, Reuters, USA Today, NY Post, STAT and Everyday Health all covered it within hours. YouTube coverage will fill up in 24–72 h, so the long-form should go out at the next 14:00 slot. The Short slots should cover the retatrutide side-effect and tolerability facts.

On other days, Lane A stays the default. Fresh hooks from this week:
- **Stopping tirzepatide:** a 39-person pilot randomized trial in Obesity Science & Practice (Oct 7, picked up by Medscape on Oct 28) found structured support was linked to slower regain. It pairs with SURMOUNT-4 and the Metabolites regain review.
- **Hair loss:** Medscape (Oct 28) reported GLP-1 hair loss looks similar across races.
- **Protein and muscle:** a J Clin Med study on device-estimated muscle loss plus Yahoo Health's "what your scale isn't telling you".
- **Plateaus:** the Türkiye cohort and the medRxiv care-patterns study.

Body-worry Shorts have fresh, checkable sources:
- tirzepatide pancreas and gallbladder: a scoping review (DMSO, Oct 23) where trial rates were lower than in adverse-event report databases
- the birth-control pill and absorption on tirzepatide (label-based, hooked to Oprah Daily, Oct 28)
- ACOG's Oct 23 guidance on pregnancy and breastfeeding
- thyroid (Newswise, Oct 28)

Seasonal: food noise around Halloween (Psychiatric Times, Oct 28), and Thanksgiving meals, which peak Nov 20–27.

Rejected: microdosing (it resurfaced via the Vogue/EMY spam feeds) and the compounded or "online" sourcing content.

Not verified: the Lilly Q3 call date, any 2026 AASLD semaglutide liver abstracts (my search only found 2025 data), and the details of the ABC "online platform stops US GLP-1 sales" story.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg: TRANSCEND-T2D-2, the first Phase 3 head-to-head (Lilly topline, Oct 28 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane C long-form, drug name first: 'Retatrutide vs Semaglutide: First Head-to-Head Results'. Open on 'you have type 2 diabetes and you're on Ozempic. Here's what this trial actually found.' Cover A1C −2.2% (9 and 12 mg) versus −1.8%, and weight −19.5%/−20.9% versus −9.4% at 80 weeks in 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin ± SGLT2. Say it was open-label, uses the 'if everyone stayed on treatment' measure, and is not yet peer-reviewed. Give the side-effect side honestly: diarrhoea 28–33% vs 26%, nausea 21–24% vs 21%, stopping because of side effects 4.8%/7.9% vs 2.7%, dysesthesia 4.8%/6.5% vs 2.7%. Retatrutide is investigational, with no approval or availability. Talk-to-your-prescriber line; no switching.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–4 days for news search; 'retatrutide vs ozempic' search stays high for weeks
candidates.why_now: Announced Oct 28 and picked up within hours by Reuters, ABC, USA Today, NY Post, STAT, BioSpace, AJMC, HCPLive and Everyday Health. It's the first randomized head-to-head of retatrutide against another incretin, and it has a semaglutide arm, so it meets every Lane C rule (≤48 h, named next-gen drug, randomized efficacy number). It matches the EloraTZP pattern that earned ~54% of our watch time.

evidence.signal: n=1,298, 2:2:1, 80 wk; A1C −2.2% vs −1.8%; weight −19.5%/−20.9% vs −9.4% (efficacy estimand); AE discontinuation 4.8%/7.9% vs 2.7%; dysesthesia 4.8%/6.5% vs 2.7%
Clinical trade pickup naming TRANSCEND-T2D-2, semaglutide 2 mg comparator
Open-label, baseline A1C 7.0–10.5%, first Phase 3 vs another incretin
Mainstream consumer pickup ('up to 60 pounds' framing; avoid this framing)

candidates.topic: Retatrutide side effects in the new head-to-head: what 'dysesthesia' (skin tingling or odd sensations) is and how often it happened (TRANSCEND-T2D-2, Oct 28)
candidates.angle: 13:00 retatrutide 'what's confirmed?' Short. In TRANSCEND-T2D-2 (type 2 diabetes, 80 weeks), dysesthesia was reported in 4.8% (9 mg) and 6.5% (12 mg) versus 2.7% on semaglutide 2 mg, and more people stopped because of side effects (4.8%/7.9% vs 2.7%). Stomach side effects were similar to semaglutide. Calm 'honest uncertainty' tone. The drug is investigational, with no approval and no legitimate online source. End on a loop.
candidates.why_now: The tolerability figures came out with the topline on Oct 28, but headlines lead with 'double the weight loss'. People will search the side effects next, and almost no creator explains dysesthesia.

evidence.signal: Financial/consumer pickup of late-stage diabetes trial

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 plus the new pilot randomized trial showing structured support was linked to slower regain (Obesity Sci Pract, Oct 7; Medscape Oct 28)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form (#3 in the playbook): 'Tirzepatide: What Happens When You Stop?' First sentence answers it: in SURMOUNT-4, people switched to placebo regained 14.0% from week 36 to week 88. Not from the start; 335 vs 335 randomized after a 783-person lead-in. Then the hopeful part: a small 39-adult pilot RCT (4 months) found ~3.6% regain with an app or medically tailored meals versus ~10.75% with usual care. It's a pilot, and both groups still regained. Add the Metabolites systematic review and the habits that help. Say clearly: 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own'.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
how to keep weight off after GLP-1
candidates.predicted_peak: Evergreen; extra lift over the next 1–3 weeks as employer coverage drops for 2027 (CNBC Oct 27)
candidates.why_now: Several independent signals on the same day: Medscape (Oct 28) on structured support, The National (Oct 28) 'what happens when the injections stop', Grocery Dive and Food Dive (Atkins targeting lapsed GLP-1 users), plus the Metabolites regain review (Oct 9). Coverage losses for 2027 will push more people to search this. It's next in the playbook's Lane A order.

evidence.signal: Pilot RCT, 39 adults: control +10.75% vs app +3.60% vs meals +3.58% over 4 months
Systematic review of weight regain after stopping GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 agonists
'Structured Support Can Slow Weight Gain in Adults Off GLP-1'

candidates.topic: Protein on tirzepatide: how much and why. Hooked to the new J Clin Med study on how much weight loss is muscle (device-estimated, Oct 15) and Yahoo Health's 'what your scale isn't telling you' (Oct 28)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form (#2 in the playbook): 'Tirzepatide Protein: How Much Do You Need?' Open on 'your appetite has dropped and you're eating half what you used to'. Cover guideline-based protein ranges for adults losing weight (as general guidance; no individual targets), why lean mass matters, the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (~75% fat / ~25% lean; Look et al. 2025; 124 vs 36 people), and easy protein-first meals when you're nauseous. Pair it with strength training. Talk to your prescriber or a dietitian.
candidates.predicted_peak: Evergreen; New Year spike from late Dec
candidates.why_now: A new J Clin Med paper on weight-loss size versus muscle loss, consumer pickup from Yahoo Health on Oct 28, and Longevity.Technology on 'protecting muscle on semaglutide'. Muscle has appeared in 6 snapshots at a steady 70–72. Practical tirzepatide long-forms earn ~2.4× channel minutes.

evidence.signal: Weight-loss magnitude, fat mass and device-estimated muscle loss during obesity pharmacotherapy
'Losing Weight on a GLP-1? Here's What Your Scale Isn't Telling You'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common is it and what helps? Fresh hook: Medscape (Oct 28) reports GLP-1-linked hair loss looks similar across races, plus the cutaneous systematic review (Med Sci Basel, Oct 9)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form (#4): 'Tirzepatide Hair Loss: How Common Is It?' Answer first: in trials it was uncommon, and much of it is likely telogen effluvium (temporary shedding) linked to fast weight loss. Then cover what real-world cohorts say (these are 'linked to', observational), why rapid weight loss and low protein matter, when to see a doctor, and reassurance that shedding of this kind usually regrows.
keywords: GLP-1 hair loss how to stop
candidates.why_now: New Medscape pickup on Oct 28. The topic has appeared in 2 snapshots, and it's in the playbook's Lane A order. Hair is a top body-worry search for women 30–60 in tier-1 countries.

evidence.signal: 'Hair Loss Associated With GLP-1 RAs Appear Similar by Race'
Systematic review of skin side effects with semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide
Matched real-world cohort linking GLP-1 RAs to non-scarring hair loss (observational)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the pancreas and gallbladder: what a new scoping review found (Diabetes Metab Syndr Obes, Oct 23) plus a propensity-matched comparison against semaglutide and DPP-4 inhibitors (J Clin Med, Oct 16)
candidates.angle: 08:00 'honest uncertainty' body-worry Short. In randomized trials, pancreatitis was uncommon (11 people across 5 studies; 0.2–3.7%) and gallstones were 0.3–3.7%. Adverse-event report databases show higher shares, but they can't measure risk. Name the warning signs on the label (severe belly pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting) and say to contact a clinician right away. Not personal advice. Separate from the gallbladder Short (10-27): this one leads with the pancreas.
candidates.why_now: Two new papers in October. The body-worry format is our best Short lane on YouTube (bones 237, nausea 153). The review was published Oct 23, and no consumer outlet has covered it yet.

evidence.signal: 11 RCTs, 5 observational studies, FAERS and EudraVigilance; RCT pancreatitis 0.2–3.7%, cholelithiasis 0.3–3.7%; calls for standardized reporting
Propensity-matched real-world comparison: tirzepatide, semaglutide, DPP-4i biliary/pancreatic safety

candidates.topic: Food noise on tirzepatide: why cravings can go quiet, and why Halloween candy may feel different (Psychiatric Times, Oct 28)
candidates.angle: Halloween-timed (Oct 31) Short, plus a possible Lane A long-form 'Tirzepatide and Food Noise: Why Cravings Go Quiet'. Explain how GLP-1 acts on the brain's appetite and reward areas, citing the evidence. Be honest: one tirzepatide study found the effect on food noise faded after a few months (small, early research). Give practical habits. No 'cure' or binge-eating treatment claims.
candidates.why_now: Psychiatric Times published on Oct 28, and Halloween is 3 days away. 'Food noise' is one of the most searched GLP-1 phrases, and it connects to the 'how GLP-1 works' pillar.

evidence.signal: 'Food Noise and GLP-1 Drugs: What Research Reveals About Motivation and Appetitive Drive'

evidence.source: PMC review (food noise, DMN and reward circuits)
evidence.signal: Review of mechanisms; peer-reviewed background

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and birth-control pills: why the label advises a backup method when starting and after each dose increase. Hooked to Oprah Daily's 'Your GLP-1 might be interfering with common medications' (Oct 28)
candidates.angle: Practical Short (and an Instagram Reel). Slower stomach emptying can affect how some oral medicines are absorbed. The tirzepatide label specifically advises people using oral hormonal contraception to switch to a non-oral method, or add a barrier method, for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase. Quote the label exactly; no dosing. Tell people to share their full medicine list with their prescriber or pharmacist and not to change anything on their own.
candidates.why_now: Oprah Daily's interaction piece ran on Oct 28. Many women in our audience don't know about this label section, and the 'Mounjaro babies' theme keeps coming back. The facts come straight from the FDA label, so the evidence is solid.

evidence.signal: 'Your GLP-1 Might Be Interfering with These Common Medications'
Case report on a possible GLP-1 interaction with a psychiatric medicine (single case; context only)

candidates.topic: Planning a pregnancy or breastfeeding on a GLP-1? What ACOG's new guidance (Oct 23, 2026) says
candidates.angle: Calm Short and Instagram Reel. ACOG says clinicians should counsel on the limited safety data and consider stopping GLP-1s 1–2 months before trying to conceive. For breastfeeding, it recommends shared decision-making and advises against use with preterm infants and newborns. Frame it as 'questions to bring to your OB or prescriber', not instructions. Quote only printed words and credit ACOG with the date (an ACOG misattribution caused a hold on 10-24). No open-question engagement lines and no emoji.
candidates.why_now: ACOG released the guidance on Oct 23. Contemporary OB/GYN (Oct 28) and NewsNation (Oct 27) are still covering it, and a new US claims study (Eur J Obstet Gynecol, Oct 15) shows exposure around conception is rising.

evidence.signal: ACOG guidance: consider discontinuing 1–2 months before conception; shared decision-making in lactation; avoid with preterm infants/neonates

evidence.source: PubMed / Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol (Oct 15)
evidence.signal: Rising exposure to anti-obesity medicines in preconception and pregnancy, US claims 2018–2023

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide weight-loss plateau: what the trials show (SURMOUNT-1 curve flattening around week 60–72) plus real-world data (J Clin Med Türkiye cohort, Oct 13; medRxiv care patterns, Oct 6)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form (#5): 'Tirzepatide Plateau: Is It Normal?' Answer first: yes. In the trials, average weight loss slowed and levelled off in the second year. Explain why (the body adapts, appetite changes) and the habits linked to better outcomes (protein, strength training, follow-up visits per the medRxiv care-patterns study). No dose-change advice; talk to your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: It's in the playbook's Lane A order and has appeared in 2 snapshots. Two fresh real-world papers in October make good hooks.

evidence.signal: Real-world semaglutide and tirzepatide weight trajectories, Türkiye
Post-initiation care patterns and weight loss with semaglutide and tirzepatide

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and drinking: what clinicians are seeing (Medscape, Oct 28) and why Heineken is warning bars (NewsNation, Oct 28)
candidates.angle: Instagram and YouTube benefit Short: 'Can tirzepatide or semaglutide change how much you want to drink?' Early randomized evidence is mostly semaglutide (a small RCT on alcohol use disorder), so keep it 'early research' and 'not an approved use'. Mention the safety point that alcohol plus vomiting means dehydration risk, and that this is to discuss with a clinician. Use semaglutide in the title only if the evidence is semaglutide-only.
candidates.why_now: Medscape and NewsNation covered it the same day, and Medical Economics and STAT did last week. The holiday season starts soon. It ties to the 'beyond weight' pillar, which works on Instagram.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1s and Alcohol Use: What Clinicians Are Seeing in Practice'
'Weight-loss drugs vs. beer: Why Heineken is warning bars'

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: protein first, smaller plates, eating slower and easier holiday meals when you get full fast
candidates.angle: Seasonal Lane A long-form plus Shorts, published by about Nov 12–18 so they rank before the peak. Use a 'you' scenario at the Thanksgiving table, with practical, nausea-friendly tips. No restriction or extreme-diet messaging; enjoy the meal.
candidates.why_now: It has appeared in 3 snapshots at a steady 70–72, with UC Davis and Men's Health guides already out. The seasonal cycle starts in 2–3 weeks, and searches peak the week of Thanksgiving.

evidence.signal: Steady momentum 70–72; UC Davis Health guide and Men's Health chef piece (Oct 26)

candidates.topic: Menopause and GLP-1s: hormone therapy linked to greater weight loss (MedPage Today Oct 27, Healthline Oct 26), plus CagriSema women's analysis
candidates.angle: Instagram Reel and YouTube Short: 'Tirzepatide or semaglutide in menopause: does hormone therapy change results?' Real-world, observational evidence, so use 'linked to'. Say that HRT decisions belong with a clinician. Positive, empowering framing for women 45–60.
candidates.why_now: MedPage Today and Healthline both covered it in the last 48 h, following the Patient Care and AARP pieces (Oct 23). Women in midlife are a core, high-value audience for us.

evidence.signal: 'Menopausal Hormone Therapy May Boost GLP-1 Weight Loss'
'Menopause: How GLP-1s and Hormone Therapy Can Affect Weight Loss'

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and the thyroid: what patients should know (Newswise, Oct 28) plus the scoping review on thyroid surveillance and cancer detection (Diabetes Res Clin Pract, Oct 27)
candidates.angle: Body-worry 'honest uncertainty' Short. Explain the boxed warning (based on rodent studies, plus who shouldn't take these medicines: personal or family history of MTC or MEN2), what human data show (mixed observational signals, possibly more detection because of more testing), and symptoms to report. No fear framing; talk to your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: A Newswise patient explainer (Oct 28) plus two new reviews (Oct 11 and 27). Thyroid is a common, long-running fear search.

evidence.signal: Scoping review: thyroid surveillance practices and possible detection bias
'GLP-1 medications and thyroid disease: What patients should know'

candidates.topic: Heart benefits of GLP-1 medicines by age: an updated meta-analysis of randomized trials (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 27)
candidates.angle: Instagram benefit Reel and Short: 'Do GLP-1 heart benefits hold for people over 65?' Report the meta-analysis findings for each age group, with absolute context where available. Mention SELECT's population (heart disease plus overweight, no diabetes) and common side effects. Check the abstract numbers before scripting.
candidates.why_now: A meta-analysis of RCTs published Oct 27 with no consumer pickup yet. Benefit Reels do best on Instagram (blood pressure 172, FLOW 124).

evidence.signal: Updated meta-analysis of RCTs: cardiovascular effects of GLP-1 RAs across age groups

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and liver disease (MASH): new meta-analysis (Medicine, Oct 23) ahead of Novo's AASLD liver data (Oct 28 press release; 2026 meeting dates unverified)
candidates.angle: 'Beyond weight' Short or Reel: what the meta-analysis says about fat in the liver and MASH resolution, the approved MASH indication for semaglutide 2.4 mg (check current US status before scripting), and who it applies to. Treat the AASLD presentation as a follow-up hook once the data are public.
candidates.predicted_peak: Around the AASLD meeting (likely early–mid Nov)
candidates.why_now: Novo's PR Newswire release (Oct 28) announces new Wegovy liver data at The Liver Meeting, and a fresh meta-analysis came out Oct 23. Fatty liver affects about 1 in 3 people with obesity.
